title: Observability and health in one screen
rememberThis: Three pillars: logs (what), metrics (how much/fast), traces (where time went) — OpenTelemetry unifies export.
Structured logging = message templates + BeginScope; never string interpolation or log secrets.
Liveness = restart if hung (self only). Readiness = route traffic (includes DB). Never put DB on liveness.
Correlation ID propagates via middleware → BeginScope → HttpClient handler → Problem Details → queue headers.
dotnet-counters monitor shows thread-pool queue and GC live — first tool for prod slowdown without restart.
bullets: AddOpenTelemetry: AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation + AddHttpClientInstrumentation + AddOtlpExporter or UseAzureMonitor.
Custom ActivitySource for business spans; filter /health from traces and reduce probe log noise.
MapHealthChecks /health/live (tags: live) and /health/ready (tags: ready); startupProbe for EF migrations.
Metrics: alert on p95 latency and 5xx rate; avoid high-cardinality labels (per-user-id on counters).
App Insights: operation_Id joins request + dependencies in transaction view; KQL for incident queries.
Distributed tracing requires traceparent on every HttpClient call — missing hop breaks the flame graph.

rows.label: Logs vs traces
rows.value: Logs = discrete events with context; traces = timed span tree with parent-child links

rows.label: Liveness vs readiness
rows.value: Liveness failure → pod restart; readiness failure → removed from load balancer, no restart

rows.label: Correlation vs trace id
rows.value: Often same (Activity.TraceId); or separate X-Correlation-Id aligned explicitly

rows.label: Prod diagnosis
rows.value: dotnet-counters (thread pool/GC) → dotnet-trace (CPU) → App Insights transaction (slow dep)

rows.label: Interview trap
rows.value: One /health with DB check on liveness; HttpClient without header propagation; $" interpolation in logs
